_comment: Drives test/klippy/multi_mcu_avr_stm32_xmcu.test under a mixed simavr (atmega2560) + renode (stm32f103) fan-out with stepper_z routed across the architecture boundary. tick_mode lockstep: klippy broadcasts each `advance T` to BOTH backends (the simavr bridge's tick socket and the renode launcher's tick socket) and waits for both `done` replies, so the two MCU clocks stay aligned with klippy's reactor - which is required for cross-MCU homing not to trip the trsync watchdog as the free-running clocks drift. Needs both the renode tick path (sentinel-delimited monitor round-trips) and the simavr tick path (synchronous host shuttle + SIGPIPE-safe control thread) working; verified 3/3 once both landed. auto_trsync_trigger_ticks fires X/Y endstops on the AVR control socket and the Z endstop on the renode launcher's control socket (renode_hooks.step_trigger drives gpioPortC[2] high after the configured rising edges on gpioPortB[0]). G28 completes with all three step_triggers cooperating. Under tick-mode lockstep the host<->mcu byte shuttle has coarse, load-jittery latency in simulated time (the renode satellite especially) versus the ~1ms of a real serial link, so test_klippy.py widens two klippy timing margins for tick-mode runs (real hardware never sets either var): KLIPPY_TRSYNC_TIMEOUT widens the 25ms multi-mcu trsync watchdog so cross-mcu homing doesn't trip 'Communication timeout during homing', and KLIPPY_MIN_REQTIME_DELTA widens the serialqueue's 100ms command pre-transmit lead so the renode-hosted stepper_z queue doesn't underrun ('Timer too close'). Together they let this test gate reliably.
